title.en: Needn't have or didn't need to

es: Distinguir needn't have + participio (se hizo sin necesidad) de didn't need to + base (no hacía falta) y leer si la acción se realizó o no.

vocabulary.es: empacar, hacer las maletas o cajas

teaching.en: We needn't have rented a van, because Carlos had a big car.
teaching.es: No hacía falta que alquiláramos una furgoneta, porque Carlos tenía un coche grande.
teaching.explanationEs: Needn't have + participio: sí lo alquilaron, pero no era necesario.
segments: We needn't have rented a van,
because Carlos had a big car.
teaching.audioText: We needn't have rented a van, because Carlos had a big car.

teaching.en: I didn't need to pay a deposit, so I kept my money.
teaching.es: No necesitaba pagar una fianza, así que me quedé con mi dinero.
teaching.explanationEs: Didn't need to + base: no hacía falta y, por eso, no se pagó.
segments: I didn't need to pay a
deposit, so I kept my money.
teaching.audioText: I didn't need to pay a deposit, so I kept my money.

teaching.en: You needn't have cleaned the flat; it was already clean.
teaching.es: No hacía falta que limpiaras el piso; ya estaba limpio.
teaching.explanationEs: Needn't have cleaned: la limpieza se hizo, pero sobraba.
segments: You needn't have cleaned the
flat; it was already clean.
teaching.audioText: You needn't have cleaned the flat; it was already clean.

teaching.en: They didn't need to carry the boxes upstairs because the lift worked.
teaching.es: No necesitaban subir las cajas por la escalera porque el ascensor funcionaba.
teaching.explanationEs: Didn't need to carry: el ascensor hacía el trabajo, así que no lo cargaron.
segments: They didn't need to carry the
boxes upstairs because the lift worked.
teaching.audioText: They didn't need to carry the boxes upstairs because the lift worked.

teaching.en: I didn't need to pack the books, so I left them on the shelf.
teaching.es: No necesitaba empacar los libros, así que los dejé en la estantería.
teaching.explanationEs: Con didn't need to, el resto de la frase suele aclarar qué pasó.
segments: I didn't need to pack the books,
so I left them on the shelf.
teaching.audioText: I didn't need to pack the books, so I left them on the shelf.

title.en: Supposed to, meant to, bound to
title.es: Se suponía que y seguro que

es: Usar be supposed to, be meant to y be bound to para hablar de expectativas, planes incumplidos y certezas, en presente y en pasado.

teaching.en: The ceremony is supposed to start at four.
teaching.es: Se supone que la ceremonia empieza a las cuatro.
teaching.explanationEs: Be supposed to + base: lo que se espera según el plan o la norma.
segments: The ceremony is supposed
to start at four.
teaching.audioText: The ceremony is supposed to start at four.

teaching.en: The band was supposed to arrive at two, but they were late.
teaching.es: La banda debía llegar a las dos, pero llegaron tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Was supposed to + base en pasado suele indicar que el plan no se cumplió.
segments: The band was supposed to arrive
at two, but they were late.
teaching.audioText: The band was supposed to arrive at two, but they were late.

teaching.en: We were meant to sit near the cake, but the table was full.
teaching.es: Se suponía que nos sentábamos cerca del pastel, pero la mesa estaba llena.
teaching.explanationEs: Be meant to + base: lo que se pretendía o estaba previsto.
segments: We were meant to sit near the
cake, but the table was full.
teaching.audioText: We were meant to sit near the cake, but the table was full.

teaching.en: With so many guests, the speeches are bound to be long.
teaching.es: Con tantos invitados, seguro que los discursos serán largos.
teaching.explanationEs: Be bound to + base: certeza sobre lo que va a pasar.
segments: With so many guests, the speeches
are bound to be long.
teaching.audioText: With so many guests, the speeches are bound to be long.

teaching.en: It was bound to rain on the day of the wedding.
teaching.es: Seguro que iba a llover el día de la boda.
teaching.explanationEs: Was bound to + base: algo inevitable visto desde el pasado.
segments: It was bound to rain on
the day of the wedding.
teaching.audioText: It was bound to rain on the day of the wedding.

title.es: Un fin de semana que se torció

es: Seguir el relato de un fin de semana fallido y distinguir si un modal perfecto expresa deducción, crítica o necesidad.

teaching.en: We missed the train; we should have left earlier.
teaching.es: Perdimos el tren; deberíamos haber salido antes.
teaching.explanationEs: Should have + participio: crítica de algo que no se hizo.
segments: We missed the train; we
should have left earlier.
teaching.audioText: We missed the train; we should have left earlier.

teaching.en: The tickets must have fallen out of my bag.
teaching.es: Seguro que las entradas se cayeron de mi bolso.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: deducción segura sobre el pasado.
segments: The tickets must have fallen
out of my bag.
teaching.audioText: The tickets must have fallen out of my bag.

teaching.en: It can't have been your fault; you were with us all weekend.
teaching.es: No puede haber sido culpa tuya; estuviste con nosotros todo el fin de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: deducción negativa, casi seguro que no.
segments: It can't have been your fault;
you were with us all weekend.
teaching.audioText: It can't have been your fault; you were with us all weekend.

teaching.en: We needn't have booked a taxi, because the bus was free.
teaching.es: No hacía falta que reserváramos un taxi, porque el autobús era gratis.
teaching.explanationEs: Needn't have + participio: se hizo, pero no era necesario.
segments: We needn't have booked a taxi,
because the bus was free.
teaching.audioText: We needn't have booked a taxi, because the bus was free.

teaching.en: The hotel might have lost our reservation.

teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posibilidad, sin estar seguro.

lost our reservation.
teaching.audioText: The hotel might have lost our reservation.

It was a bad idea.
It was not necessary.

hint.es: Piensa si el hablante adivina, critica o dice que sobraba.

origin.text: The tickets must have fallen out of Mia's bag.
